facts.statement: The genus Eosuchus was named in 1907 based on a fossil specimen discovered near the Belgian border in northern France.
facts.quote: The name Eosuchus was first used in 1907 to describe a single specimen found from northern France near the Belgian border, assigned to the type species Eosuchus lerichei.

facts.statement: The species Eosuchus minor was originally discovered in 1870 by Othniel Charles Marsh but was initially classified under the genus Gavialis.
facts.quote: A second species, Eosuchus minor, was actually discovered earlier in 1870 by Othniel Charles Marsh, but was assigned to the genus Gavialis.

facts.statement: The species name 'minor' reflects an estimated maximum length of 2 meters, which is significantly smaller than the modern gharial that can reach 5 meters.
facts.quote: The species name minor refers to the relatively small estimated size of the animal, estimated at no more than 2 meters, when compared to other gavialoids such as the modern gharial, which can grow up to 5 meters in length.

facts.statement: In 1986, the name Thecachampsoides was proposed for the species formerly known as Gavialis minor.
facts.quote: The new generic name Thecachampsoides was proposed for the species G. minor in 1986.

facts.statement: The name Eosuchus was officially applied to the specimens of Thecachampsoides minor in 2006.
facts.quote: it was not until 2006 that the name Eosuchus was applied to the T. minor specimens

facts.statement: Fossils of Eosuchus have been found in France and in eastern North America, specifically in Maryland, Virginia, and New Jersey.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from France as well as eastern North America in Maryland, Virginia, and New Jersey.

facts.statement: Concave depressions on the skull bones of E. lerichei suggest it possessed salt glands and was capable of tolerating saltwater environments.
facts.quote: The internal surface of the prefrontal and lacrimal bones of E. lerichei are characterized by concave depressions, which in several marine lizards, iguanas and birds are where salt glands are housed, suggesting this species was capable of saltwater tolerance.

facts.statement: A fossil oyster was found attached to the snout of an E. minor specimen, indicating it may have lived in shallow marine waters.
facts.quote: One specimen of E. minor from the Aquia Formation, USNM 299730, has a fossil oyster attached to the dorsal surface of the rostrum.

facts.statement: Recent studies suggest Eosuchus may not be a gavialoid or crocodylian, but rather a non-crocodylian eusuchian.
facts.quote: The authors considered it most likely that Eosuchus was not a gavialoid, or even a crocodylian, but rather a member of the clade of non-crocodylian eusuchians

facts.statement: Eosuchus is often classified as a 'thoracosaur,' a group of basal gavialoids that do not form a true evolutionary clade.
facts.quote: Eosuchus is often referred to as a "thoracosaur", a group that was constructed to include many basal forms of gavialoids that cannot be placed into any specific families of their own, yet do not form a true clade.

facts.statement: Eosuchus minor is distinguished from Gavialis by a narrow, smooth interfenestral bar on the parietal bone.
facts.quote: Another diagnostic feature thought to distinguish the species from Gavialis was the narrow interfenestral bar of the parietal bone that is relatively smooth and unsculptured when compared to other gavialoids such as Thoracosaurus.

facts.statement: E. minor and E. lerichei share similarities including a large foramen aerum, a long nasal process, paired dentary alveoli, and a W-shaped basioccipital tuberosity.
facts.quote: The examination of specimens of Thecachampsoides minor with those of Eosuchus lerichei yielded many similarities between the two species, including the foramen aerum as well as other features such as a long nasal process between the premaxillae, dentary alveoli arranged in pairs, and a W-shaped basioccipital tuberosity.

facts.statement: E. minor differs from E. lerichei by having a wider nasal bone and prefrontals positioned further forward on the skull than the lacrimals.
facts.quote: E. minor differs from E. lerichei on the basis of a noticeably wider nasal and prefrontals positioned anteriorly further up the skull than the lacrimals.

facts.statement: Eosuchus is distinct from other gavialoids because it retains a thin descending lamina next to the pterygoid bone.
facts.quote: The genus is distinct from gavialoids in still having a thin descending lamina positioned next to the pterygoid.

facts.statement: Recent reevaluations suggest E. lerichei is the more basal species and likely the ancestor of E. minor in Europe.
facts.quote: A recent reevaluation of the holotype material of E. lerichei, which in the past has been poorly studied, suggests that it is the more basal species and thus would have been the ancestor of E. minor in Europe.

facts.statement: The genus name Eosuchus was first used in 1907 to describe a single specimen found in northern France near the Belgian border, assigned to the species E. lerichei.
facts.quote: El nombre Eosuchus fue utilizado por primera vez en 1907 para describir un solo espécimen encontrado del norte de Francia, cerca de la frontera belga, asignando el nombre a la especie E. lerichei.

facts.statement: A second species, E. minor, was named in 2006 based on material found in the United States that had previously been referred to various different crocodile genera.
facts.quote: Una segunda especie, E. minor, fue nombrada en 2006 con material encontrado de los Estados Unidos, habiendo sido referido en el pasado a varios géneros diferentes de cocodrilos.

facts.statement: E. minor differs from E. lerichei based on a notably wider nasal and prefrontal bone positioned above the skull, in front of the lacrimal bones.
facts.quote: E. minor difiere de E. lerichei sobre la base de un notablemente más ancho hueso nasal y prefrontal, posicionados por encima del cráneo, antes de los lagrimales.

facts.statement: Examination of specimens revealed many similarities between the two species, including the pneumatic foramen, a long nasal bone between the premaxilla, jaw alveoli arranged in pairs, and a W-shaped basoccipital tuberosity.
facts.quote: El examen de los especímenes de T. minor con los de E. lerichei arrojó muchas similitudes entre las dos especies, incluido el foramen aerum, así como otras características tales como un largo hueso nasal entre el hueso premaxilar, los alvéolos de la mandíbula dispuestos en pares y una tuberosidad basoccipital en forma de W.

facts.statement: The genus lived during the Thanetian to Ypresian stages, approximately 59.24 to 48.07 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Thanetian to Ypresian (59.24 to 48.07 million years ago)

facts.statement: Eosuchus belongs to the parent group Gavialoidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Gavialoidea

facts.statement: Eosuchus is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Eosuchus is E. lerichei.
facts.quote: Type species: Eosuchus lerichei

facts.statement: The strata containing both Eosuchus species are believed to have formed in a marginal marine depositional environment, likely reflecting the real habitats these animals inhabited.
facts.quote: Los estratos a partir de los cuales se han encontrado ambas especies de Eosuchus se cree que se formaron en un ambiente marginal de deposición marina, y, por lo tanto, probablemente reflejen los entornos reales que habrían habitado estos animales.

facts.statement: A specimen of E. minor from the Aquia Formation (USNM 299730) has a fossil oyster attached to the dorsal surface of its snout.
facts.quote: Un espécimen de E. minor de la Formación Aquia, USNM 299730, tiene una ostra fósil unida a la superficie dorsal del rostro.

facts.statement: A recent re-evaluation of the holotype material of E. lerichei suggests it is a more basal species and would have been the ancestor of E. minor in Europe.
facts.quote: Una reciente revaluación del material holotípico de E. lerichei, que en el pasado había sido poco estudiado, sugiere que es una especie más basal y, por lo tanto, habría sido el antecesor de E. minor en Europa.

facts.statement: It is currently accepted that a close relationship between Eosuchus and tomistomines is not the case, and that similarities between them may be superficial, representing primitive traits lost in more derived members like modern Gavialis.
facts.quote: A pesar de esto, actualmente se acepta que una relación estrecha entre Eosuchus y los tomistominos no es el caso, y que las similitudes entre los dos pueden ser superficiales y que estas características son plesiomórficas para todos los gavialoideos, perdiéndose en miembros más derivados tales como el Gavialis moderno.

facts.statement: Both Eosuchus and tomistomines possess a deeply concave deltopectoral crest, unlike the more triangular crests found in Gavialis.
facts.quote: tanto Eosuchus como los tomistominos tienen una cresta deltopectoral profundamente cóncava, a diferencia de las crestas más triangulares de Gavialis.

rejected.quote: The strata from which specimens have been found date back to the late Paleocene and early Eocene epochs.
